summary: Farzand Ali Durrani was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Peshawar (~1956–1958), the University of the Punjab, and the University of London (~1961–1964). He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar (~1968–1993).
Fausto Gherardo Fumi (1840–1915) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore's Classe di Lettere e Filosofia under Giuseppe Bardelli from circa 1858 to 1862.

Fawad Khan is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master's in Archaeology at the University of Peshawar, completed his PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, and was an Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (attested 2022).

Fazun (1902–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Taixu, Dayong, and Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, among others, and at Drepung Monastery. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and later served as president and director at the Buddhist Academy of China.

Federico Squarcini is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held positions at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (~2011), served as Series Editor for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (~2012), and joined the editorial board of Marco Polo (~2021).

Feng Youlan (1895–1990) was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University and Columbia University. He held an academic post at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952) and served as a visiting professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947).
Ferdinand Benary (1805–1880) studied under Franz Bopp from circa 1827 to 1829. In 1831, he was appointed extraordinary professor in the theological faculty at the University of Berlin.

Ferdinand Christian Baur (1792–1860) was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Tübingen and the Tübinger Stift (~1809–1814) and later served on the faculty at the University of Tübingen (~1826–1860).

Ferdinand Diederich Lessing (1882–1961) was a scholar in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He taught at the University of Berlin and the University of California, Berkeley, and his students included Alex Wayman, Helmut Hoffmann, and Wolfram Eberhard.

Ferdinand Hitzig (1807–1875) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829). He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and the University of Heidelberg (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi (1837–1907) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and completing his Habilitation at Marburg, he served at Marburg as associate professor (1865), full professor (1869), and Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing (1882–1961) was a Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Berlin (1902–1905). He held posts at Peking University (1919–1921), the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (~1930–1935), and UC Berkeley (~1935–1960).

Ferdinand Sommer (1875–1962) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg. He held professorships at Basel (1902), Rostock (1909–1913), Jena (1913–1924), Bonn (1924–1926), and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure (1857–1913) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig under Curtius and Brugmann, then taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1881–1891) and as professor at the University of Geneva (1891–1913).

Ferdinand von Eckstein (1790–1861) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1810–1812), became a member of the Société Asiatique (~1823–1861), and founded the journal Le Catholique in 1826.

Ferenc Ruzsa (born 1957) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He completed his education at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1977–1982), and he taught Gergely Hidas.
Fernand Meyer is a Tibetologist who held positions at the CNRS and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 2004). His students include Marc-Henri Deroche and Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy.
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Nalanda University, completing his doctoral research under Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola (1915–2017) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the National University of San Marcos (~1933–1944). He taught at the University of Buenos Aires (~1970–1984) and directed the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).
The Fifth Karma Kuchen (born 1970) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Penor Rinpoche as a heart son and succeeded him in 2000.
